validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED as a real corridor, but NOT by the sheet's own citations. The gem.wiki page's only two refs are OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 (p.75) and ASB2013 (p.79) -- generic country-aggregate pipeline-length tables that do NOT name any 'Tanajib-Berri' line (both opec.org URLs also 403 to the verifier now). Every P1897-P1925 Saudi row was batch-created 2022-07-19 with the same reused ASB citation, so the OPEC ref is a placeholder, not support. Independent confirmation instead comes from Fluor (the EPC contractor that built Aramco's Berri/Shedgum/Ju'aymah gas plants): its Offshore Gas Gathering System page states gas from Safaniya/Marjan/Zuluf was 'transported by pipeline to shore at Safaniya and Tanajib' and 'from there ... transported along the coast to processing facilities ... at Berri, Shedgum and Ju'aymah' -- i.e. a Tanajib->Berri gas transport line genuinely exists. Aramco's own 'Master Gas System -- fueling a nation' article carries the identical description (a 2nd, non-GEM source), but aramco.com/aramcolife URLs time out on the verifier so I do not cite them. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- raw/associated GAS feeding the Berri Gas Plant, not oil/NGL/condensate, not plant-internal; a legitimate gas line (part of the northern-area gathering->MGS network). DUPLICATE: none found. No other roster row originates at Tanajib; the other Berri-terminating rows have different origins (P1921/P7768 Abu Ali, P1898/P1899 UBTG-1, P1906 Abqaiq, P1916 Qatif North, P1922/P1923 Berri->Abu Ali). GulfPub's 20-feature Saudi gas roster (the best-covered country) has NO Tanajib entry, so no relabel collision -- but that absence also means GulfPub cannot corroborate the specs. ATTRIBUTION: Owner Saudi Aramco 100% is correct (all MGS/gathering infra is Aramco). FuelSource 'Tanajib Copmplex' is right in substance (gas comes ashore/through the Tanajib complex) but has a typo. SPEC: Length 145 km is geographically plausible -- Ras Tanajib (~27.87N 48.77E) to Berri GP at Jubail (~26.95N 49.59E) is ~130 km straight-line, consistent with ~145 km along a coastal routing -- but neither 145 km nor 30-in diameter is independently corroborated; Fluor gives only a system-wide '150+ miles of various-diameter pipelines' figure, not this segment. So specs stay single-sourced (medium/low), not a material disagreement, hence caveat not concern.

routes.corridor_desc: Runs roughly south-southeast for ~145 km along the Saudi Persian Gulf coast, from the Tanajib/Ras Tanajib onshore complex (near Manifa, ~130 km NW of Jubail) down to the Berri Gas Plant in Jubail Industrial City. It is part of Aramco's northern-area offshore gas gathering network that lands gas at Safaniya/Tanajib and moves it along the coast to the Berri/Shedgum/Ju'aymah gas plants (Fluor). Endpoints are well established; the exact intermediate routing is not publicly sourced, so the corridor is bounded to the coastal strip between Tanajib and Jubail. Straight-line endpoint distance (~130 km) is consistent with the stated 145 km.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from named facilities: Ras Tanajib complex (coord ~27.869N,48.768E, from the Ras Tanajib airport/complex geolocation) and the Berri Gas Plant at Jubail (~26.954N,49.586E, from public facility geolocation). Corridor direction/length confirmed by Fluor's description of coastal gas transport from Tanajib to Berri. No intermediate coordinates fabricated -- waypoint left null and described in words. Suggest medium (not high) because exact route geometry is unsourced.

summary: P1904 Tanajib-Berri: real Aramco gas corridor (Fluor-confirmed), correctly classified, no duplicate, Owner Aramco correct -> confirmed (caveat); specs 145km/30in single-sourced, FuelSource typo, sheet's OPEC ASB refs don't name it.
